Thanks, Sam — quick technical plan and recommended integration steps so the kickoff is productive. High-level approach: use Redwood hosted sandbox with streaming generation + function/tool calling to hit your ticketing endpoint for automated ticket creation and KB retrieval for RAG.

1) Authentication & sandbox creds
- We'll provide an API key scoped to the Acme sandbox project. Use standard header: Authorization: Bearer <KEY>.

2) SDK & endpoints
- Recommended: our Node SDK for fastest iteration; fallback to curl for quick tests. Primary generation endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
- For streaming: use the same endpoint with header Accept: text/event-stream or via our SDK stream() helper.

3) Tool-calling (ticket creation flow)
- Redwood supports function/tool calling: model can return a structured call to a registered tool. We'll register a tool for your ticketing system that makes an HTTP POST to https://acme.ticketing.internal/api/v1/tickets/create with payload {title, description, metadata}.
- Flow: user -> Redwood generate (with tools enabled) -> model returns tool call -> Redwood runtime executes tool (optionally in sandbox to prevent side effects) -> returns result to model -> model finalizes response.

4) KB integration for RAG
- Two options: hosted vector DB (we can ingest the CSV) or you host embeddings endpoint; for POC we'll ingest sample CSV into our sandbox index. We provide an ingestion script that calls POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -> store vector index and configure retrieval.

5) Telemetry & metrics
- We'll emit token-level latency, per-request SLOs, and per-route cost estimates to the console and a short JSON payload to your webhook: POST https://hooks.acme.com/redwood/metrics (optional). Sample metrics available during POC: median latency, 95p latency, tokens per request, tool-call success rate.

6) Rate limits & expected throughput
- Sandbox default: 5 concurrent streaming sessions; for POC this should be enough. For higher parallelism we can increase cap for the trial.

7) Sample code (Node)
- const {Redwood} = require('@redwood/inference');
- const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY});
- const stream = await client.generate.stream({model: 'redwood-1.0', input: 'Find the latest ticket for order #123', tools: ['acme_ticket_creator']});

8) Next steps before kickoff:
- Acme: share sandbox key request + sample CSV
- Acme: confirm ticketing API auth method (API key or OAuth) and a test endpoint that allows create in sandbox mode
- Redwood: provide sandbox key + ingestion script + temporary dashboard link with metrics

I'll bring a runbook and a quick demo to Monday's call. Ping me if you want a short pre-kickoff sync.

— Dev
